hook: There is no lead in your pencil.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, warm workshop light on cedar wood and dark glinting graphite, soft yellow and grey palette
world: Pencil making from a misty 1500s English hillside to a bright modern factory, warm light on wood and graphite
through_line: the dark graphite core, from a black rock on a hillside to the tip of a finished pencil

props.Pencil: a plain yellow hexagonal wooden pencil with a pink eraser and a sharp tip showing a dark grey core, no markings
props.Graphite rock: a fist-sized lump of shiny black-grey graphite rock with a metallic glint
props.Cedar slat: a flat pale cedar wood board with eight parallel grooves, a thin dark rod lying in each groove

places.Hillside: a misty green English hillside in the 1500s, grey stone walls, grazing sheep
places.Factory: a clean pencil factory floor with steel machines, conveyor belts and warm work lights

captions.hook_line: There has never been any lead in a pencil. Here's what's really inside ✏️
captions.body: Pencil 'lead' is graphite mixed with clay, pressed into rods and fired in a kiln, then glued between grooved cedar slats and sliced into pencils. A big graphite find in 1500s England was mistaken for lead, and the name stuck. More clay makes a harder, lighter line; more graphite a softer, darker one.

sources.claim: Pencil cores are graphite mixed with clay; graphite found in Borrowdale, England in the 1500s was mistaken for lead; more clay makes harder pencils

blocks.narration: There is no lead in your pencil. There never was. It is graphite and clay, baked hard like pottery.

blocks.narration: In the fifteen hundreds, shepherds in England found a shiny black rock. They called it lead, and the name stuck.
blocks.visual: A shepherd in a wool cloak kneeling on the misty Hillside, pulling the Graphite

shots.visual: A shepherd in a wool cloak kneeling on the misty Hillside, pulling the Graphite rock out of the earth
beats: he lifts the rock into the light

beats: the rock drags across the wool

blocks.narration: Today, powdered graphite and clay are mixed into a dark dough, pressed out into long thin rods, and fired in a hot kiln.
blocks.visual: Steel paddles churning thick dark grey paste in a big Factory mixing drum

shots.visual: Steel paddles churning thick dark grey paste in a big Factory mixing drum
Thin dark rods sliding out of a steel nozzle onto a Factory conveyor, perfectly straight
beats: a rod pushes out of the nozzle

shots.visual: Trays of thin dark rods rolling into a glowing orange kiln in the Factory
beats: the tray slides into the heat

blocks.narration: Here is the trick. More clay makes a harder, lighter line. More graphite makes it softer, darker, and smudgier.
blocks.visual: The Pencil drawing a crisp pale grey line across white paper

shots.visual: The Pencil drawing a crisp pale grey line across white paper
beats: the tip glides across the paper

shots.visual: The Pencil drawing a thick rich black line, then a thumb smudging it
beats: a thumb smears it into a cloud

blocks.narration: The rods are glued between two grooved slats of cedar, then a blade slices the sandwich into pencils. No lead anywhere.

A spinning blade slicing the glued Cedar slat into a neat row of yellow Pencils that roll apart
